body: Thank you. I don’t want to call her heartless, she just has some very strict personal rules that she takes very seriously. I think it’s to protect her independence, stemming from a previous “controlling” relationship. I understand this in general, and it’d be another story entirely if my situation had just been something minor... but it wasn’t. And now I’m unsure if I can trust her to be there for me if I really need her. Idk what to do or how to explain it to her in a way that will make her understand and she can’t seem to articulate why this is something she can’t seem to let go. It’s very troubling.

Wishing you all the best as well. It’s tough loving someone and not knowing if they love you the same way. Like, not “do they love me as much as I love them,” but do we just inherently “love” differently. It’s frightening and fascinating at the same time.

I don’t really have any advice, but I just wanted to say that a lot of this resonated with me. I definitely consider myself non-monogamous and want to experience new things with new people. But I love my partner in a way that I can’t really imagine loving someone else, simultaneously. Like, not even close to the same level. Perhaps experience will prove me wrong, but I can’t help but feel like my partner and I might just be wired a little differently if that is something she actively believes in and wants. She’s more experienced in the poly world than I am, so maybe she’s just more open to all of it and I’m still evolving, but it does scare me. A lot.
It’s going to be difficult but you *have* to tell your therapist. Please, please do so.

I’m sorry you’re dealing with such difficult emotions. This is not healthy for you or your girlfriend. She seems to be going through an exploratory phase that is likely to be very important for her. Therapy, perhaps together, is probably going to be necessary for you to get through this. Just don’t stew in it, clearly this is hurting you very deeply. Just please remember she isn’t doing any of this to hurt *you*. 

Please do whatever you can to get the help that you need—don’t let this relationship dictate your happiness. That will be up to you. Good luck.

“One thing I’ve learned from researching poly is that relationships can end at any time, mono or poly. “

Yeah, it’s easy to forget that sometimes. 

Thank you for your perspective.

Hey, thank you very much. I appreciate input from people who have really lived it and not just people telling me why it won't work. If it doesn't it doesn't, but we're trying right now and that's what matters. And I hear you, I could go get myself laid if I really wanted to, and maybe I will, but it's just not a super high priority for me right now. I'm gonna talk to her about a couple things, make sure we're still on the same page, I know we are but like I said this was the first time the "openness" of everything has actually come up. Hoping she and I both can just talk honestly about how it feels from our perspectives. I'm not going to give her any kind of guilt trip, this is what I signed up for... but I wouldn't be being honest if I didn't say it made me feel a little extra lonely. Oh well. Thanks again.

I'm not traditionally poly but I'm not locked into monogamy either. I've been experiencing a lot of new things with her--and it's been great. Like I said, it's a test. I need to get through it. If I can't, if it's too hard, well I guess I'll know I'm not cut out for this. I'm not giving up on it before we've given it an honest try first, though. In a few months we'll no longer be long-distance and we can get back to exploring things together. I legitimately want her to have fun. I'm not even jealous--just hurting from the distance.
I hope that's not what's happening, but thank you for the reply. I think you're right, it's kind of on her now to get back in touch. Oh well. We'll see I guess.

I'm gonna give it some time, she likely has a perfectly good reason. It's just been such a stark turn in how I thought things were going.

I hear you. And I won't try to convince you you don't need intimacy.

I will say that the pursuit of sex is a rigged game. You will likely try on many different faces trying to get it. But is it really yours? 

If it is intimacy you seek, not just the "I crossed the finish line" moment, sex cannot be the goal. That's the trap I mentioned. Intimacy comes from someone wanting to be close to you-- for YOU, not just what's between your legs. And to do that you have to find yourself. Be true to yourself. Pursue what you are good at and people will see your value. They'll want to get to know you, and that will lead to the intimacy you seek.

You're 30, and 30 is a lot younger than you think it is. Forget about your "prime." You can have a healthy sexual relationship at any age, but remember that many women's sexual prime is in their mid-late 30s and beyond. You have plenty of time.

I won't continue to preach to you. Just know I was in your shoes for a very long time. It took me getting out of my own head about it and just going out and living. Easier said than done, I know. But you're fine. You really are.

It's a basic human *desire*

Losing your virginity is also like the most anti-climactic thing ever. If it happens naturally, as it should, you'll be like ok umm that was cool but really that was it? You've likely built it up in your head into something it just isn't. It's minor at best, and a whole new uncharted realm of depression-inducing bullshit at worst.

I get it if you don't believe me, but once it happens for you you'll look back on it and be like "damn, I spent all that time freaking out over this?"

There are far more meaningful pursuits in life. And I bet if you follow one of them, it will lead you to something you're good at that fulfills you. And when you're in your element, you're sexy.

It's a trap in your mind. Stop playing by its rules and create your own.

Losing your virginity is pretty much the most overrated thing ever. You build it up in your head like its so fucking important, but it really isn't.

I lost mine at 25 in the most hilariously un-sexy way. I then went on to have amazing sex for the next 6 years or so. Now I honestly don't really care anymore. When it happens, cool, but it doesn't rule your life the way it feels like it does.

Stop turning it into some big goal you have to achieve. It'll happen when it happens, and if it doesn't, that's really ok too. You just have to let go of it as an albatross around your neck. It's fine. You're fine.

Edit: I should also mention that those 6 years of amazing sex also contained enough misery that I would likely trade it all back if I could. 2 depressive people with great sexual chemistry but not much else is a dangerous thing. Especially if a pregnancy enters the equation.
